context_needed: SPIR-II midline report (Gilligan et al. 2024), Amhara and Oromia, Ethiopia. Arms (PDF page 7 and Table 2.1): T1 = control, PSNP transfers only; T2 = SPIR-II programming plus nurturing care groups; T3 = T2 plus maternal cash transfers to pregnant and lactating women. Randomised by kebele; estimates are intent-to-treat by assignment. Round: midline. Units: knowledge score points (row 1), percentage points (rows 2-4), HAZ z-score (row 5). The definition of 'conditional' is in the table note on page 83. The running header says 'Baseline Survey Report' but this is the midline report.

rule: When a table shows the same outcome with and without controls (unconditional / conditional, unadjusted / adjusted), store both, one row each, and name the version in specification. Mark preferred: true only when the authors say which one is their main estimate. Arm contrasts printed as 'T2-T1' go into arm as a named comparison, never into the outcome. A row that contrasts two programme arms (for example T3 minus T2) is stored with effect_type 'difference between arms', naming both arms in arm.

resolved_questions.question: Are arm-versus-arm contrasts (T3-T2) wanted?
resolved_questions.resolution: Decided by Lucas, 22 Nov 2026: yes, stored with effect_type 'difference between arms'.

resolved_questions.question: (1) The authors never call either specification preferred: the report's figures show the unconditional estimates and the text says the conditional ones are 'similar', so no row carries preferred: true. (3) Rows 2-5 do not say '(ANCOVA)' in their headers; the note says ANCOVA is used whenever a baseline value exists, so the specification labels leave it out for those rows.
